description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various probing methods applied to multilingual BERT models, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The vertical axis represents accuracy, ranging from 70 to 95, with major gridlines at intervals of 5. The horizontal axis lists different probing configurations, grouped into categories: “embedding,” “1st layer,” “random layers” (with subvariants: +B₂, +L₂, +R₂, +permute), “random” (with same subvariants), and “unperturbed.” Each group contains two bars: a lighter-colored bar (light gray, light blue, light green, or light red) and a darker-colored bar (dark blue, dark green, or dark red), likely representing two different experimental conditions or model variants. Accuracy values vary across conditions: “embedding” and “1st layer” show moderate performance (~82–83), “random layers” variants hover around 80–82, “random” variants are significantly lower (~71–73), and “unperturbed” achieves the highest accuracy (~90–92). The chart visually emphasizes that unperturbed models outperform all perturbed configurations, and that probing deeper or randomized layers generally degrades performance compared to early layers or embeddings. The bars are not sorted by value but grouped by probing strategy, with color coding distinguishing paired conditions within each group.
